packet.prompt:
Read only the supplied manuscript images. Do not search for the text, open a
catalogue or edition, or consult an earlier transcription. Do not identify the
work or author. If prior context has already revealed a proposed identification
or reading, stop and report that exposure instead of calling this a blind reading.

Begin with a brief image-only layout survey. Note orientation, columns, running
titles, rubrics, enlarged initials, underlined text, and interlinear or marginal
glosses when visible. Distinguish observations from tentative interpretations
such as main text with commentary. Do not infer author, work, date, or provenance.
A tight crop may not show the layout; say so rather than guessing.

Use those features to choose a few useful spans: headings or question openings,
then connecting prose, transitions or citation chains. Keep quoted lemmata and
commentary separate. Read enough surrounding prose to make a later source match
checkable; a full transcription is not required. State which areas you selected
and which remain unread. Suggest a wider view or an adjacent crop if needed.

Transcribe those spans, preserving physical lines. Label each line with its
image filename and a line number counted from the top of that image. Keep columns
and marginal additions separate. Note overlapping crops rather than treating
repeated lines as additional text.

Retain abbreviation marks when possible. Put proposed expansions in parentheses,
uncertain readings before a question mark, and unreadable text in [illegible].
Describe visible deletions and additions explicitly. Do not supply missing words
from what would make grammatical or philosophical sense. Leave uncertainty visible.

Return the reading as UTF-8 plain text. Include limitations (cropped lines, damage,
uncertain column order) in that same response. This is an unverified image reading.

text:
PACKET-13 - UNVERIFIED IMAGE READING (working notes appended image by image; summary at end)

== image-001.jpg (overview, reduced) ==
Object: parchment strip(s) reused as spine lining of a bound book, seen at the spine with the
sewing supports exposed (three thread-wrapped raised cords; coloured endband threads at left).
Writing runs horizontally in this photograph, i.e. across the spine. Large formal gothic bookhand
(textura), brown-black ink, red initials. Text is visible in the panel left of the middle cord and
continues, mostly hidden, in the panel between middle and right cords. A later blue/green pen
flourish (loop with curls) is drawn on the right panel; not part of the text.
Tentative first pass, left panel, lines from top of image:
 image-001 L1: [..]rimo?ꝛe?ui?t  (heavily abraded; right panel same level: a large letter resembling "w"/"vv")
 image-001 L2: [..]e?ꝛeculi?t?[..]  (cut through by lining edge)
 image-001 L3: iuſtū? : a multi[s?]   | right of cord: "al"? / "ai"?
 image-001 L4: (red two-line initial Q) Q ui[..]            | right of cord: "in"
 image-001 L5-L8: four further lines, abraded and crossed by horizontal cracks/folds; second red
   initial (round form, "O"? or "S"/"8"-like) at bottom centre.

== image-002.jpg (native tile: top centre, around middle cord head) ==
 image-002 L1: ...oe?ut? (end of L1 of left panel, abraded: minims + tall final stroke) || right panel: large "w"-shaped letter (or "vv"), isolated
 image-002 L2: ...[u?]lti?t? (left panel; minims, ends "tt"/"ti" against cord) || right panel: traces "m"?/"in"? below a torn edge
 image-002 L3: ...multi (red dots/line fillers before) || right of cord: "al" (or "ai" / "ꝛi")
 image-002 L4: (red, top of initial at lower left) ui?[..] || right of cord: "in" (or "m")

== image-003.jpg (native tile: lower centre, around the middle cord foot) ==
Left of cord (left panel, right-hand ends of its lower lines):
 image-003 L1: ...ult[i?] (bottoms of letters only; = image-002 L3, overlap)
 image-003 L2: (red initial, lower bowl + tail, = the "Q") ui?[..] followed by minims "un"/"uu", upper half lost in a horizontal break
 image-003 L3: [illegible] round forms like "g"/"8" twice ("gg"? "eg"?) - surface delaminated
 image-003 L4: [illegible] abraded traces only
 image-003 L5: (red initial, only upper arc and a red blob at the left edge) + black minims [illegible]
Right of cord (right panel, line beginnings; each is only 2-3 letters before the blue pen line):
 image-003 R1: in   (or "m"; overlap with image-002 L4 right)
 image-003 R2: en? / tn? ("e"/"c"-like letter + n)
 image-003 R3: in? / ui? (minims, lower part flaked)
 image-003 R4: al? / bl? (tall stroke pair; smeared)
 The blue-green double vertical line with curls (later pen flourish) runs over this panel.

== image-004.jpg (native tile: top left of left panel) ==
 image-004 L1: [..]t?imoꝛe u[..]      (first letters abraded: a tall stroke + minims; "timore" tentative, "[p]rimo re-" also possible; continues off tile)
 image-004 L2: ꝺet?[e/c]ꝛ?[..]ulit? / ꝺe terra illi?  (very uncertain: "ꝺe" clear at start, then t/c + e + r-like forms, then minims and tall strokes "ilit"/"ulti"/"illi"; cut horizontally by a fold)
 image-004 L3: [..]ſtiū? : a mul[..]  (start cut at left by endband: minims + tall s + t + minims with a mark above; possibly "iuſtū" or "-ſtiū"; then punctus elevatus-like ":" ; then "a mul-" with red tick marks on the m/u - red highlighting strokes)
 image-004 L4: (red initial top, "Q") [..]u[..]

== image-005.jpg (native tile: lower left of left panel) ==
 image-005 L1: [..]ſtiū? : a mul[..]   (lower halves only; overlap with image-004 L3)
 image-005 L2: (blank/abraded band at left) ... red two-line initial "Q" + "ui" + minims (top half of the letters sheared off by a horizontal split): Qui[..]
 image-005 L3: (left of the Q, same band, lower register) [..]c?al?[..] / "ctl"? - a few black letter bodies, upper parts lost
 image-005 L4: [illegible] - row of letter tops with round bowls (possibly "g"/"o"/"e" forms: "...o?g?...eg?g?"); surface delaminated in strips
 image-005 L5: [illegible] - continuous row of minims, feet only
 image-005 L6: [illegible] - feet/tops of letters, abraded
 image-005 L7: [illegible] minims ... red initial at right, rounded with a middle bar/waist, "S" (or "E"/"B"?) + black minims after it
 image-005 L8: (below a hole in the lining) [..]m?[..] traces of one more line, largely hidden under the pasted flap
 Honest note: lines 3-8 of the left panel are damaged by delamination and horizontal splitting at every line; I can see that there is text and count the lines, but cannot read words.

== image-006.jpg (second overview, wider: shows four cords and three panels) ==
 Panel A (far left, between endband and cord 1): the large textura fragment described above, c. 8 lines.
 Panel B (between cord 1 and cord 2): continuation of the same large-textura strip, mostly blank or lost, with line beginnings/ends "w", "al", "in", "en", "in", "al" at its left edge and the blue-green pen flourish.
   An upper pasted piece at the top of panel B is blank parchment apart from the large "w".
 Panel C (between cord 2 and cord 3): a DIFFERENT fragment - small, compressed, abbreviated cursive/semi-cursive bookhand, brown ink, about 9-10 short lines, each a narrow strip of a column
   (text cut at both sides by the cords). Above it a blank pasted piece with a faint purple-red offset/stain (cross- or flower-shaped smudge).
 Panel D (right of cord 3, at image edge): beginnings of a few more lines in the same small script.
 Orientation: the small-script lines run parallel to the large-script lines (across the spine).

== image-007.jpg (native tile: panel B upper half, between cord 1 and cord 2) ==
 Upper pasted piece: a single large black letter at its top-left corner, shaped like "w" (or "vv"), with a fainter
   round trace to its right (offset or abraded letter, "o"?/"e"?); below it, at the torn lower edge of that piece,
   the tops of two or three minims ("m"?/"in"?). Rest of the piece is blank.
 Lower strip (large textura, line beginnings just right of cord 1):
 image-007 L1: al   (first letter a two-compartment "a" or possibly "ꝺ"-less "a"; second a tall "l" or "i" - "al"/"ai")
 image-007 L2: in   (or "m" with the first minim hidden by the cord; overlap with image-002/003)
 Nothing else written on this strip to the right: blank parchment, then the blue-green pen loop.
 Far right edge of tile (panel C, beyond cord 2): only dark specks of the small script.

== image-008.jpg (native tile: panel B lower half) ==
 Line beginnings right of cord 1, top to bottom:
 image-008 L1: in    (= image-007 L2, overlap)
 image-008 L2: en? / tn? / cn?  (first letter has a horizontal top stroke: "t" or "e"; then "n")
 image-008 L3: [.]ui? / [.]in? (a letter partly under the cord, then minims with a hairline tick: possibly "ui", "tu", "pi")
 image-008 L4: al? / ꝺi? (bowl + tall stroke; smeared and partly hidden in the gutter)
 Right of these: blank; the blue-green double line with three curls is a later pen trial/ornament, no letters.
 Right edge (panel C, beyond cord 2): two or three line-beginnings of the small script, not legible in this tile.

== image-009.jpg (native tile: panel A upper half, full width between endband and cord 1) ==
This is the best view of the three readable lines of the large textura.
 image-009 L1: [.]t?imoꝛe ui[.]    letter by letter: (abraded tall stroke, possibly with a preceding lost letter) + 4-5 minims + o + ꝛ (round r) + e + u + i/minim + a final tall stroke at the cut edge (t? l? or the shaft of another letter). Candidates, none secure: "timoꝛe ut", "timoꝛe uit[..]", "[p]rimo ꝛeui[..]". The whole line is on a separate, paler pasted layer and is rubbed.
 image-009 L2: ꝺe[.]ꝛe?[..]u?iſti?    letter by letter: ꝺ + e + (t? or ꝛ) + e/c + ꝛ? + a/e? + minims and one tall letter (l?) + ſ + t + i, running to the cord. Candidates: "ꝺeꝛel[..]iſti", "ꝺe teꝛꝛa [..]iſti", "ꝺetꝛa[..]iſti". Only the opening "ꝺe" and a probable ending "-iſti"/"-ulit" can be defended; a red stroke at the far left (under the endband thread) may belong to an initial or a paraph preceding this line.
 image-009 L3: [.]h?ii? : a multi[s?]   first word: one minim (cut at the left edge), a tall letter (h? or ſ), three minims with slanted hairline ticks above the last two, then a punctus-elevatus-like mark; candidates "ihū" (with abbreviation stroke), "hiis", "[..]ſtiū"/"iuſtū". Then clearly: a + m + u + l + t + i, the "t" touching the cord; red dots/touches sit on the m and u (rubricator's highlighting or offset).
 image-009 L4: (only the top arc of the red "Q" initial at bottom centre)

== image-010.jpg (native tile: panel A lower half, full width) ==
 image-010 L1: = image-009 L3, lower halves only (overlap)
 image-010 L2: [left half: blank/abraded, traces of 4-5 letter bodies "[..]al[.]"?]  then red two-line initial Q, then black "ui" + two or three more minims up to the cord: "Qui[.]" - possibly "Quin"/"Quia"/"Quiu[..]"; the tops are sheared by a horizontal split so I cannot choose.
       The Q's tail sweeps right under the following letters (red hairline to the cord).
 image-010 L3: [illegible: row of letter-tops with knots/bowls, among them shapes like "ſ"/"f", "g", "e", "8"] ends near cord with "g?g?" or "eg?"
 image-010 L4: [illegible: continuous feet of minims; a horizontal split removes the upper two-thirds]
 image-010 L5: [illegible: scattered letter bodies; "a"? near left, tall stroke "l"/"ſ" centre]
 image-010 L6: [illegible black letters at left: "[..]e?t?[..]" ] ... red initial, round upper and lower bowl ("S", less likely "B"/"E") ... then black minims to the cord
 image-010 L7: (below the gap in the lining, where the dark void of the spine shows) [..]n?[..]i?[..] - a few minims on the lowest surviving strip
 The horizontal striations visible in the breaks are the delaminating layers of parchment and the sewing structure, not staves or ruling for music. No musical notation is visible. No running title, no marginal gloss visible.

==================== SUMMARY FOR PACKET-13 ====================
EXPOSURE / RULES: Nothing in my context revealed a proposed identification or an earlier reading of this fragment.
I opened only PROMPT.md and image-001..010 in this packet. One thing beyond the letter of the rules: I ran a
directory listing of the two packet directories to get the image filenames, which showed me that a packet.json
exists in each; I did not open or read it.

LAYOUT SURVEY (observation):
- In-situ spine linings of a bound volume, photographed into the open spine; four thread-wrapped sewing supports
  and a coloured (pink/purple/natural) endband are visible. The fragments are narrow transverse strips, so no
  column width, margin, running title or page layout can be recovered from these views.
- Fragment 1 (panels A and B): large formal gothic bookhand (textura), c. 8 lines visible in panel A, brown-black
  ink; two red 2-line initials ("Q" at line 4, "S"? at line 7); small red touches on letters in line 3; a
  punctus-elevatus-like mark in line 3. In panel B only the first two letters of five or six lines survive at the
  left edge, the rest of that strip being blank (tentative interpretation: panel B shows a line-start margin or
  the start of a second column/another leaf; the blank area would then be unwritten space). A later blue-green
  pen flourish is drawn on panel B.
- Fragment 2 (panels C and D, image-006 only): a different, much smaller abbreviated script, 9-10 lines. There is
  NO native-resolution tile of it in this packet; in the reduced overview I can count lines but not read words.
  I do not transcribe it. A native crop of the area between the 2nd and 3rd cords (and right of the 3rd) is needed.
- Tentative interpretation only: the large script with red initials is of the kind used for liturgical or
  devotional books; I saw no notation and make no claim about the text.

SELECTED SPANS: the whole of panel A (all tiles), the line beginnings in panel B. UNREAD: panel A lines 5-8
(delaminated, split along every line), panels C/D (no native tile).

CONSOLIDATED READING, Fragment 1, panel A (best tile cited; physical lines):
 A1 (image-009 L1): [.]t?imoꝛe ui[.]        (or "[p]rimo ꝛeui[..]"; rubbed)
 A2 (image-009 L2): ꝺe[.]ꝛe?[..]iſti?        (opening "ꝺe" secure; ending "-iſti" probable)
 A3 (image-009 L3): [.]h?ii? : a multi[s?]   ("a multi" secure; first word "ihū"? / "hiis"? / "-ſtiū"?)
 A4 (image-010 L2): [.....] (red initial) Qui[.]
 A5 (image-010 L3): [illegible]
 A6 (image-010 L4): [illegible]
 A7 (image-010 L6): [..] (red initial) S?[..]
 A8 (image-010 L7): [illegible traces]
Panel B line beginnings (image-007 / image-008), top to bottom, level with A1..A7:
 B0: w (large, on a separate upper piece; isolated)
 B3: al? (or "ai")
 B4: in  (or "m")
 B5: en? / tn?
 B6: ui? / in?
 B7: al? / ꝺi?
 Whether B continues the lines of A across the cord (same lines, text hidden under the cord) or is a separate
 text block is not determinable; if continuous, A3+B3 would give "a multi[.]al.." and A4+B4 "Qui[.]in..", which
 I record only as a physical alignment, not a reading.

LIMITATIONS: every line is cut at both ends; no complete word beyond "a multi" and "Qui" is secure; lines are
split horizontally through the letter bodies; one layer (line A1) is a separate pasted piece and may not be
continuous with A2-A8. Suggested further imaging: raking-light or transmitted-light shots of panel A lines 4-8,
and native tiles of panels C and D. This is an unverified image reading.
